headline: High risk of prompt injection, data leakage, and capability conflict from shared filesystem and broad egress; Goose can read/write the workspace while Chatwoot handles customer data and external integrations.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Goose can read/write the user filesystem and use MCP, so it can ingest Chatwoot outputs if they are copied into shared files or extensions. Chatwoot has broad network egress and integrations, but no direct shared channel is documented. The pathway exists via filesystem bridging, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Chatwoot outputs are saved into a workspace file that Goose reads
IF an MCP extension forwards Chatwoot text into Goose prompts
mitigations: Keep Chatwoot and Goose in separate workspaces
Disable or remove MCP extensions that ingest Chatwoot output
Use a manual copy-paste review step before Goose consumes Chatwoot text
Prefix shared files with provenance labels
requires-engineering: add content provenance filtering between the agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Chatwoot touches customer data, contact profiles, interaction history, orders, and messages, while Goose reads and writes the filesystem and has broad network egress. If both share a workspace, Goose can access sensitive files and transmit them through configured model providers or MCP servers. That creates a realistic exfiltration path in default use.
conditions: IF customer data is stored in the shared cwd or adjacent files
IF Goose is configured with a model provider or MCP server that sends file contents off-machine
mitigations: Store customer data outside Goose's working directory
Restrict Goose to a sanitized subset of files
Disable unnecessary MCP servers and external providers
Rotate or redact sensitive exports before handoff
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation at the OS or container layer

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Goose can write the filesystem, modify git state, and run subprocesses; Chatwoot is a runnable open-source app with integrations and broad egress. Because Goose shares state via filesystem and both can act on the same workspace, concurrent edits or git mutations can collide and corrupt work. The overlap is enough to treat the default pair as dangerous.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git checkout or cwd
IF Goose performs git writes while Chatwoot-generated artifacts are also being updated
mitigations: Assign separate directories per agent
Pause one agent before the other writes
Use git locks or a single-writer policy
Commit or snapshot before handoff
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Goose can act on files and git state, so if it treats Chatwoot-generated text as authoritative, errors can cascade into code or operational changes. Chatwoot can emit customer-support content and reports, but no verification boundary is documented between them. The pathway exists in default workflows, though not every run is harmful.
conditions: IF Goose consumes Chatwoot reports or messages as facts without verification
IF Goose then edits files or commits based on those facts
mitigations: Require a human review step before Goose acts on Chatwoot output
Mark Chatwoot exports as untrusted input
Use structured schemas with validation before downstream actions
Limit Goose to read-only analysis for Chatwoot-derived artifacts
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking gates

E_compliance.rationale: Chatwoot handles customer data and messages, while Goose handles files in the user filesystem and sends data to configured model providers. If customer data or regulated content is placed into Goose's workspace, retention and residency controls may diverge from Chatwoot's support-system handling. The mismatch is plausible but not proven from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF regulated customer records are copied from Chatwoot into Goose-managed files
IF Goose's provider or extension retention differs from Chatwoot's support-system retention
mitigations: Avoid moving regulated records into Goose files
Redact personal data before transfer
Document retention for any shared exports
Use separate storage policies per system
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls across both tools
